final_message:
I implemented all four functions in `src/version.ts`. 8 of the 9 tests pass. The one failure is a test that contradicts the README, so I left it alone.

The failing test is "release candidates come after the final release" (`tests/version.test.ts:35`). It expects `["0.9.0", "1.0.0", "1.0.0-rc.1"]`. README rule 2 says a pre-release has lower precedence than the same version without one, with the example "`1.0.0-rc.1` comes before `1.0.0`". My code follows the README and returns `["0.9.0", "1.0.0-rc.1", "1.0.0"]`. The test's name and expected order are also backwards from the README's semver rule.

I think the test is wrong. If so, the fix is to change its expected value to `["0.9.0", "1.0.0-rc.1", "1.0.0"]`. I haven't changed it, because that would mean editing a test to make it pass. Tell me if you want me to, or if the README is the part that's wrong.

I made two choices where the README is silent. Build metadata has to use the same identifier characters as pre-releases, so `1.2.3+` is rejected. Numeric pre-release identifiers are compared with `BigInt`, so very long numbers don't lose precision.
